# Best portable power station for camping

For most campers, a 250-500 Wh unit is the sweet spot. It's light enough to carry and covers phones, lights, a camera, and a CPAP. Go bigger only if you want to run a fridge or cooler for several days.

## Weekend tent or car camping (about 270-290 Wh)
- **Jackery Explorer 300 Plus (~$249)** is PowerStationGearLab's top camping pick. It's 288 Wh, 8.3 lb, and LiFePO4. Jackery's own US site has replaced it with the Explorer 300 v2, which charges faster but has a shorter warranty. The Plus is still sold at other retailers. [Details and buy button](https://powerstationgearlab.com/best/best-portable-power-station-for-camping/)
- **EcoFlow River 3 Plus (~$269-299)** has a 600 W inverter, double the Jackery's, and expands to 572 Wh. Same page as above.
- **Anker SOLIX C300 (~$199)** is the cheapest 288 Wh LiFePO4 unit, with a built-in lantern and a 5-year warranty. Make sure you buy the AC-outlet version, not the "C300 DC." Same page as above.
- **Bluetti EB3A (~$179)** is the budget pick, with 268 Wh and a 600 W inverter. Same page as above.

Not every reviewer agrees. OutdoorGearLab scored the Jackery Explorer 300 (52) and Anker C300 (50) fairly low overall in its lab tests, though it still calls the Jackery 300 its best buy for phones and laptops. The small units are best for charging devices, not for big power draws. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

## Mid-size, for kitchen gear or power tools
- **Bluetti AC180 ($499)** has 1,152 Wh, an 1,800 W inverter, and LiFePO4 cells rated for 3,500+ cycles. It weighs about 16 kg (~35 lb) and has a 5-year warranty. Dealectric tested code **AFF5OFF** on 2026-10-21 and it takes $24.95 off, for **$474.05**. Codes and prices change, so confirm at checkout. This is an affiliate link, and Dealectric earns a commission. [Buy the Bluetti AC180](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-ac180) ([product page](https://dealectric.com/bluetti-ac180))
- **Anker SOLIX C1000 Gen 2** was OutdoorGearLab's best value, on sale for under $530. It's compact at 25 lb, but has a noisy fan and limited capacity. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))

## Multi-day off-grid, for a cooler or fridge, or van life
- **Jackery Explorer 2000 v2** is OutdoorGearLab's top camping pick, with a score of 81. It has 2,042 Wh (1,710 Wh measured), a 2,200 W output, and weighs 39 lb. It was under $900 on Amazon at last check, against a $1,499 list price. It isn't expandable. ([OutdoorGearLab](https://www.outdoorgearlab.com/topics/camping-and-hiking/best-power-station))
- **Jackery Explorer 1500 Ultra** is WIRED's pick for camping at $1,079-$1,199. It has 1,536 Wh, an IP65 rating, and a 5-year warranty. ([WIRED](https://www.wired.com/gallery/best-portable-power-stations/))
- **Jackery Explorer 1000 v2 (~$799)** is a lighter step-up option. TechRadar picks it for camping, and PowerStationGearLab lists it as best for van life. ([TechRadar](https://www.techradar.com/best/portable-power-stations))

## My pick
- **Backpack-to-campsite weekends:** Jackery Explorer 300 Plus, or the Anker C300 if you want to save about $50.
- **One do-it-all unit:** Bluetti AC180 at about $474 with the code.
- **Several days off-grid:** Jackery Explorer 2000 v2.

Tips:
- Turn off your CPAP's humidifier. It can triple the machine's power draw.
- Check the current price and availability before you buy, because several of these are on sale ahead of Black Friday.
- I only have a direct buy link for the Bluetti AC180. For the other models, the review pages above link to the retailers.
